title: Scleroderma-Like Skin Changes and Multifocal Muscle Thickening in a Patient with Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Paraneoplastic rheumatic manifestations may precede the diagnosis of an occult malignancy and closely mimic primary autoimmune connective-tissue diseases. Scleroderma-like manifestations have rarely been reported in association with lymphoid malignancies, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Case presentation A 47-year-old woman presented with progressive skin thickening, difficulty walking, reduced appetite, and weight loss. She had been diagnosed with scleroderma by an outside physician in early 2024 and had been treated with methotrexate 15 mg once weekly. Physical examination revealed facial skin tightening, sclerodactyly, skin induration extending to the wrists and elbows, and asymmetric thickening of the right neck, forearm, and thigh muscles. Pruritic migratory annular plaques were observed on the trunk and resolved spontaneously within two weeks, clinically suggesting an erythema annulare centrifugum-like eruption. Raynaud phenomenon was absent, antinuclear antibody testing was negative, and cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy was present. Computed tomography demonstrated multiple destructive osteolytic lesions in the lumbar vertebrae. Neck magnetic resonance imaging showed edema-like T2 hyperintensity involving the sternocleidomastoid muscle and adjacent tissues without contrast enhancement. Biopsy of a vertebral lesion revealed DLBCL, with tumor cells positive for leukocyte common antigen and CD20 and a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 80%. The patient was started on standard first-line R-CHOP immunochemotherapy but died in the intensive care unit after the first treatment administration, precluding assessment of treatment response and longer-term follow-up. Conclusion This case illustrates an unusual presentation of DLBCL accompanied by scleroderma-like cutaneous changes, multifocal muscle thickening, and an annular eruption. The simultaneous absence of Raynaud phenomenon and antinuclear antibodies, together with constitutional symptoms, lymphadenopathy, asymmetric soft-tissue abnormalities, and destructive bone lesions, should prompt reconsideration of presumed systemic sclerosis and evaluation for an underlying malignancy. Although a paraneoplastic association was strongly suspected, it could not be confirmed because the patient died after the first treatment administration, precluding assessment of the rheumatic manifestations after lymphoma-directed therapy.

title: Comparisons in Analgesic Effects Between Ultrasound-Guided Erector Spinae Plane Block and Ultrasound-Guided Modified Intercostal Nerve Block in Modified Radical Mastectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Introduction Postoperative acute pain is a common challenge after breast cancer surgery. This randomized controlled trial compared the analgesic effects of ultrasound-guided erector spinae plane block (ESPB) and modified intercostal nerve block (MINB) in patients undergoing unilateral modified radical mastectomy. Methods Seventy patients were randomly allocated to ESPB or MINB group. The primary outcomes were the 6-hour postoperative resting and movement-evoked Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) scores. Secondary outcomes included resting and movement-evoked VAS scores at 0, 3, 12, and 24 hours, intraoperative opioid consumption, rescue analgesic use within 72 hours, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at 24 hours, and hospital stay. Results At 6 hours postoperatively, both resting VAS (median 2 [0-2] vs 2 [2-3], P=0.005) and movement-evoked VAS (median 3 [2-4] vs 4 [3-4], P=0.015) were lower in the MINB group. Resting VAS scores at 0 and 3 hours were comparable between groups. Movement-evoked VAS scores were lower in the MINB group at all post-surgery time points (P<0.05 for all). Intraoperative remifentanil consumption was lower in the MINB group (P<0.001). Fewer patients required rescue analgesics in the MINB group (P=0.038). No significant difference was observed in QoR-15 scores between groups (P=0.055). Conclusion Ultrasound-guided MINB was associated with lower 6-hour resting and movement-evoked pain scores and reduced intraoperative opioid consumption compared with ESPB, without compromising recovery quality in patients undergoing unilateral modified radical mastectomy. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2300077956; https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.aspx?proj=77956). Registered on November 24, 2023. Principal investigator: Guanghong Xu.

title: Liposomal Bupivacaine Combined with Bupivacaine vs Ropivacaine for Paravertebral Blockade in Single-Port Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery: A Propensity-Matched Comparison of Postoperative Opioid Use.
abstract: Objective To compare the effect of preoperative single-injection paravertebral block using liposomal bupivacaine/bupivacaine mixture versus ropivacaine on cumulative postoperative opioid consumption in patients undergoing thoracic surgery. Methods This retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent elective single-port video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (wedge resection, segmentectomy, or lobectomy) between January 2024 and February 2026. Patients received an ultrasound-guided single-injection paravertebral block with either 0.5% ropivacaine (20 mL) or a mixture of 1.3% liposomal bupivacaine (10 mL) and 0.5% standard bupivacaine (10 mL). The primary outcome was cumulative postoperative opioid consumption throughout the hospitalization, delivered via patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) and converted to oral morphine milligram equivalents. Secondary outcomes included pain scores, time to first PCA request, postoperative adverse events, and length of stay. Propensity score matching (1:2) was performed to balance baseline clinical and intraoperative characteristics. Results Among 492 eligible patients, 331 received ropivacaine and 161 received liposomal bupivacaine/bupivacaine combination. After matching, 210 and 108 patients were included in the ropivacaine and liposomal bupivacaine groups, respectively. The median cumulative postoperative opioid consumption was lower in the liposomal bupivacaine group (92.1 mg [IQR, 59.1-122.3]) than in the ropivacaine group (226.2 mg [IQR, 170.2-260.0]), with a median difference of 128.2 mg (95% CI, 111.0-143.9; P < 0.001). The liposomal bupivacaine group was also associated with lower resting and movement pain scores at 24 and 48 hours postoperatively, a longer time to first PCA press (26.0 vs. 6.0 hours; P < 0.001), and a lower incidence of postoperative dizziness (21.3% vs. 34.3%; P = 0.017). Conclusion For patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery, preoperative single-injection paravertebral blockade with liposomal bupivacaine/bupivacaine mixture was associated with lower cumulative postoperative opioid consumption and lower early postoperative pain scores than ropivacaine.

title: Added Prognostic Value of MRI to CT in Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients Undergoing Mechanical Thrombectomy in the Extended Time Window.
abstract: Background In the 6-24-hour window, imaging must identify patients with salvageable tissue while avoiding delays and reperfusion of large established infarcts. The optimal imaging strategy remains controversial. Although computed tomography (CT) is widely used because of its accessibility and speed, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides more sensitive tissue characterization. This study evaluated whether adding MRI to CT was associated with clinical outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) undergoing mechanical thrombectomy (MT). Methods We conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study of consecutive patients with AIS due to large vessel occlusion who underwent MT between January 2022 and December 2024. Patients were grouped according to pre-procedural imaging: CT alone or MRI plus CT. Propensity score matching (1:1) was used to reduce measured baseline imbalances. The primary outcomes were excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-1) and 3-month mortality; symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (SICH) was the secondary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted associations. Results After propensity score matching, 364 patients (182 pairs) were included in the final analysis. Compared with CT alone, the MRI plus CT group demonstrated significantly lower 3-month mortality (7.1% vs 18.7%, P < 0.01) and reduced incidence of SICH (2.2% vs 7.7%, P = 0.02). No significant difference was observed in excellent functional outcome at 3 months between groups. Multivariate logistic regression confirmed that MRI plus CT was independently associated with lower risks of mortality (adjusted OR=0.32, 95% CI 0.14-0.72; P < 0.01) and SICH (adjusted OR=0.23, 95% CI 0.05-0.96; P =0.04). Conclusion Among patients with AIS undergoing MT within the 6-24-hour window, MRI plus CT was associated with lower 3-month mortality and SICH than CT alone, without a significant difference in excellent functional outcome. Because imaging allocation was non-randomized and quantitative infarct-core and perfusion data were unavailable, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require prospective multicenter validation.

After propensity score matching, 364 patients (182 pairs) were included in the final analysis. Compared with CT alone, the MRI plus CT group demonstrated significantly lower 3-month mortality (7.1% vs 18.7%, P < 0.01) and reduced incidence of SICH (2.2% vs 7.7%, P = 0.02). No significant difference was observed in excellent functional outcome at 3 months between groups. Conclusion

Among patients with AIS undergoing MT within the 6-24-hour window, MRI plus CT was associated with lower 3-month mortality and SICH than CT alone, without a significant difference in excellent functional outcome. Because imaging allocation was non-randomized and quantitative infarct-core and perfusion data were unavailable, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require prospective multicenter validation.

title: MRI-Based Intratumoral and Multi-Range Peritumoral Radiomics for Predicting Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis in Breast Cancer.
abstract: Background To determine the best-performing peritumoral boundary among tested distances and evaluate the predictive value of preoperative multiparametric MRI radiomics for axillary lymph node metastasis (ALNM) in breast cancer. Methods Clinical and imaging data of 273 patients from two centers were retrospectively analyzed. ROIs were manually delineated on Fs-T2WI and DCE-MRI images, and peritumoral regions were generated by expanding the tumor ROI by 3 mm, 5 mm, and 7 mm. Patients from Center 1 (n = 201) were randomly divided into training and internal validation set (7:3), while Center 2 (n = 72) served as the external validation set. LASSO regression and an SVM classifier were used to construct predictive models. A nomogram integrating the best-performing radiomic model with clinical parameters was developed. Model performance was assessed using AUC and DCA. Results Maximum tumor diameter was identified as an independent risk factor for ALNM (OR = 4.042, 95% CI: 2.488-6.532; P < 0.001). Among the tested peritumoral margins, the 5 mm model demonstrated the best predictive efficacy, significantly outperforming both 3 mm (AUC 0.694) and 7 mm (AUC 0.717) models (DeLong test, all P < 0.05). The fusion model combining DCE-MRI intra- and peritumoral (5 mm) features with Fs-T2WI intratumoral features achieved AUCs of 0.909, 0.818, and 0.768 in the training, internal validation, and external validation sets, respectively. The nomogram integrating the fusion model with maximum tumor diameter further improved performance, with AUCs of 0.943, 0.884, and 0.853, respectively. Conclusion Among the tested distances, a 5 mm peritumoral margin provided the best predictive performance for ALNM. The multiparametric MRI radiomic model effectively predicts ALNM and offers a valuable non-invasive tool for preoperative assessment.

title: Evaluation of PDA‑PLL Nanoparticles for siRNA Delivery and ROS Scavenging in Rat Osteoarthritis.
abstract: Introduction Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent chronic inflammatory disease in which elevated TNF-α and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) play central roles. These two pathological factors mutually reinforce each other-TNF-α induces ROS production while ROS upregulates TNF-α expression-forming a vicious cycle that propels disease progression. However, current therapies offer only symptomatic relief without halting this process. To address this, we developed polydopamine-poly(L-lysine) (PDA-PLL) nanoparticles as a dual-functional platform that combines PDA-mediated ROS scavenging with PLL-facilitated TNF-α siRNA delivery. Methods PDA-PLL nanoparticles were synthesized and systematically characterized, and then their gene transfection efficiency and ROS scavenging capacity were evaluated. Finally, their therapeutic efficacy against OA was assessed in chondrocytes and in animal models. Results Biocompatibility was evidenced by low in-vitro cytotoxicity and the absence of systemic toxicity in rats by hematology, biochemistry, and histopathology. Agarose gel electrophoresis demonstrated their strong nucleic acid loading capability, and fluorescence imaging further revealed that PDA-PLL nanoparticles enabled highly efficient gene transfection in OA chondrocytes. PDA-PLL nanoparticles exhibited dose-dependent scavenging of O 2 •-, • OH, and H 2 O 2 in cell-free assays and lowered intracellular ROS in OA chondrocytes; critically, co-delivery of TNF-α siRNA further reduced ROS versus PDA-PLL alone. Consistent with these findings, the PDA-PLL+TNF-α siRNA group showed stronger suppression of inflammatory genes, greater restoration of matrix-preserving genes, and enhanced cytoprotection compared with PDA-PLL alone. In rat OA, PDA-PLL+siRNA outperformed PDA-PLL alone, with macroscopic and histological outcomes approaching the sham group. Conclusion This work presents PDA-PLL nanoparticles as a multifunctional therapeutic system that unites efficient gene delivery with potent ROS scavenging. Their synergistic action resulted in significant protection of chondrocytes and potent therapeutic efficacy in OA models.

title: Staged Management of Recurrent Obstructed Hemivagina in Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich Syndrome: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: Background Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome (HWWS) is a rare congenital Müllerian anomaly characterized by uterus didelphys, obstructed hemivagina, and ipsilateral renal anomaly. Recurrence after prior surgical treatment is particularly rare. We report a complex recurrent case of obstructed hemivagina in a patient with HWWS and duplicated vagina, successfully managed with a staged surgical approach. Case presentation A 19-year-old woman with a history of two prior vaginal septum resections and excision of a perineal mass (histopathology confirming ectopic colonic tissue) presented with recurrent pelvic pain and fever. MRI and endoscopic assessment demonstrated uterus didelphys, duplicated cervices and vaginas, complete obstruction of the right hemivagina, ipsilateral renal agenesis, and a deeply recessed obstructed cavity containing purulent fluid. Because of the markedly distorted postoperative anatomy, a staged surgical strategy was adopted. The first stage involved hysteroscopic and vaginoscopic decompression with ultrasound-guided septal incision and drainage. The second stage consisted of definitive reconstruction, including resection of the accessory blind tract, obliteration of the residual obstructed cavity, and perineal reconstruction. The patient recovered uneventfully, resumed regular painless menstruation. No recurrence of hemivaginal obstruction was observed during follow-up.However, the diagnosis was not definitive. The patient had lifelong persistent urinary incontinence that showed no improvement after surgery. Although a right ectopic ureter or ureterocele was unlikely to account for the continuous leakage because the right kidney was nonfunctioning, a left ectopic ureter and other lower urinary tract abnormalities had not been fully excluded. Conclusions This case highlights a complex recurrent presentation of HWWS and emphasizes the importance of MRI and endoscopic evaluation in delineating atypical postoperative anatomy. Individualized staged surgical management may help prevent re-obstruction, control infection, restore functional genital tract continuity, and preserve future reproductive potential in patients with complicated or recurrent HWWS. Persistent urinary incontinence and a history of perineal ectopic colonic tissue warrant further urological and multidisciplinary evaluation, a left ectopic ureter and other lower urinary tract abnormalities should be carefully evaluated in this patients.

title: A Case Report of a Giant Mucinous Cystadenoma Suspected to Be Associated with Ovarian Remnant Syndrome After Bilateral Adnexectomy: Diagnostic Pitfalls and Implications for Clinical Management.
abstract: Background Mucinous cystadenoma of the ovary is one of the common benign ovarian neoplasms. Nevertheless, when a huge pelvic mass develops years after bilateral adnexectomy, determining its tissue origin and establishing a differential diagnosis poses substantial challenges, complicating the clinical management of such secondary pelvic lesions. Case presentation This study reports a rare case of a giant pelvic mass occurring many years after bilateral adnexectomy in a 65-year-old Han Chinese female. Intraoperative exploration and postoperative histopathology confirmed the lesion as an ovarian mucinous cystadenoma, which was presumed to arise from residual ovarian tissue after previous surgery, consistent with ovarian remnant syndrome (ORS). However, the ovarian origin of this lesion was comprehensively determined based on prior surgical records, intraoperative findings, and histopathological morphology, without further confirmation by definitive immunohistochemical staining. Conclusion Ovarian remnant syndrome should be considered in the differential diagnosis of de novo pelvic masses following bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. A review of prior surgical records is essential for tracing the origin of such lesions. For pelvic mucinous lesions, gastrointestinal and appendiceal origins should be prioritized for exclusion, accompanied by comprehensive characterization of pathological features. To minimize the risk of long-term postoperative lesions, complete resection of all ovarian tissue should be pursued during bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy in routine clinical practice.

title: Construction of a Nomogram Integrating Magnetic Resonance Imaging Features and Ephrin-A3 Expression to Predict Postoperative Overall Survival in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Purpose Elevated EFNA3 mRNA is associated with poor prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of Ephrin-A3 immunohistochemical expression and construct a nomogram combining MRI features and Ephrin-A3 expression for postoperative OS prediction in HCC. Patients and methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of 111 HCC patients, from whom MRI data were collected, and Ephrin-A3 immunohistochemistry was performed. Using an optimal cut-off value of averaged optical density (AOD) derived from Ephrin-A3 staining to predict OS, patients were categorized into high and low expression groups. The cohort was randomly split into training (70%) and validation (30%) sets. Univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses identified independent OS predictors, and a nomogram was constructed to predict post-surgical OS. We assessed the model's performance through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, area under the curve (AUC) measurements, Kaplan-Meier survival curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA) in both datasets. Results Ephrin-A3 expression, tumor margin, nonrim arterial phase hyperenhancement, and extrahepatic metastasis were independent predictors of OS. The nomogram had concordance indexes of 0.76 and 0.72 in the training and validation sets, respectively. Time‑dependent ROC analysis showed AUCs of 0.790 and 0.776 at 36 and 60 months in the training set, and 0.737 and 0.770 in the validation set; the 12‑month AUC was not estimable due to zero events in the validation set. Kaplan-Meier curves showed significantly prolonged OS in the low-risk group across both datasets. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and actual survival rates, and DCA supported the model's clinical utility. Conclusion Ephrin-A3 serves as an independent prognostic factor for OS in HCC patients after surgery, and the constructed nomogram exhibits favorable predictive performance for postoperative survival.

title: Negative Correlation Between ADC Values and GPC3 Expression in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Quantitative Diffusion-Weighted Imaging Study.
abstract: Objective To investigate the association between apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) derived from diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and glypican-3 (GPC3) expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and to explore the potential of ADC as a non-invasive imaging biomarker for assessing GPC3 expression. Methods This retrospective study included 468 patients with pathologically confirmed HCC who underwent preoperative liver magnetic resonance imaging between January 2020 and December 2025. Based on immunohistochemical staining, patients were classified into three groups: GPC3-negative (GPC3-, n=69), low-expression (GPC3+, n=42), and high-expression (GPC3++, n=357). Tumor ADC values, adjacent liver tissue ADC values, and tumor-to-liver ADC ratios were measured and compared among groups. Statistical analyses included the Kruskal-Wallis test, Mann-Whitney U -test with Bonferroni correction, and Spearman correlation analysis. Results Tumor ADC values differed significantly among the three groups (p<0.001), with median ADC values of 1.40 (1.34-1.46), 1.35 (1.28-1.42), and 1.27 (1.23-1.31) ×10 -3 mm 2 /s in the GPC3-, GPC3+, and GPC3++ groups, respectively. The tumor-to-liver ADC ratios were 0.97 (0.94-1.00), 0.91 (0.88-0.94), and 0.87 (0.84-0.90), respectively, and also showed significant differences among groups (p<0.001). ADC values and ADC ratios were negatively correlated with GPC3 expression levels ( r =-0.52 and r =-0.56, respectively; both p<0.001). Conclusion Higher GPC3 expression in HCC was associated with lower tumor ADC values. Quantitative DWI-derived ADC, including both tumor ADC and the tumor-to-liver ADC ratio, may serve as a promising imaging biomarker associated with GPC3 expression, potentially offering supportive information for preoperative evaluation of HCC.

title: MRI-Based Radiomics Predicts FAP Expression and Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: To develop a Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) -based radiomics-clinical model for noninvasive prediction of fibroblast activation protein (FAP) expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and to explore its association with tumor microenvironment (TME) characteristics and potential immunotherapy response. This retrospective study included 104 patients with HCC from the Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University, 31 external MRI cases from The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA), and 363 transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Immunohistochemistry (IHC) assessed FAP expression. Tumor regions were manually segmented, and radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics. Multiple machine learning classifiers were used to construct and validate models for predicting FAP expression. Logistic regression was selected for its balanced performance between the training and validation cohorts, with the smallest area under the curve (AUC) difference among the five machine-learning algorithms. A radiomics-clinical combined model was further developed by integrating the radscore with clinical indicators. Radiogenomic analysis explored radscore-related transcriptomic features and immune infiltration characteristics. In the validation cohort, the AUC values of the intratumoral, peritumoral, and intratumoral + peritumoral radiomics models were 0.757, 0.502, and 0.784, respectively. The intratumoral + peritumoral model also achieved a sensitivity of 0.692 and a specificity of 0.788, indicating the best overall discriminatory performance among the three models. The radiomics-clinical combined model integrating the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), prognostic nutritional index (PNI), and radscore achieved an AUC of 0.816 in the validation cohort. Radscore-related transcriptomic modules identified 10 hub genes for risk stratification. Patients in the high-risk group exhibited a more pronounced immunosuppressive TME and poorer predicted benefit from immunotherapy. The MRI-based radiomics-clinical model effectively predicted FAP expression in HCC. Radscore reflected FAP-related immunosuppressive TME remodeling and may provide insights into potential immunotherapy response stratification, which requires further validation in independent immunotherapy-treated cohorts.

title: Viral Hepatitis, Potential Aflatoxin B1 Exposure, and Projected Metabolic Risk Factors for Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Somalia: A Call for Integrated Prevention, Surveillance, and Research.
abstract: This commentary is a narrative synthesis of Somali, regional, and global evidence on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in Somalia; it does not report new epidemiological data, and claims are graded according to whether they are directly demonstrated in Somalia or inferred from broader African or global literature. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major cause of cancer mortality globally and presents a particularly difficult challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, where chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, hepatitis C virus (HCV), food-borne aflatoxin exposure, limited surveillance, and restricted access to curative treatment intersect. Somalia has no mature population-based cancer registry, yet available hospital-based evidence indicates that liver cancer is an important component of the national cancer burden. Directly documented Somali evidence is limited to hospital case series and to donor-, hospital-, and laboratory-based HBV studies: a Somali series of 268 patients with HCC documented a predominantly male population, a relatively young mean age, large tumors, and portal-vein thrombosis associated with poor prognostic features, and recent Mogadishu studies have shown continuing HBV transmission and important gaps in vaccination, testing, and linkage to care. By contrast, the contribution of aflatoxin B1 exposure and of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) to HCC in Somalia is not directly documented. No Somali biomonitoring, dietary-exposure, or MASLD-prevalence data exist; the discussion of these pathways in this commentary is therefore inferred from regional and global literature and should be read as a precautionary, hypothesis-generating projection of future risk rather than an established local driver of current disease. This commentary argues that Somalia should nonetheless not address viral, toxic, and metabolic exposures through isolated programs. An integrated, phased HCC prevention strategy should combine timely HBV birth-dose vaccination, maternal screening and antiviral prophylaxis, adult testing and treatment, HCV diagnosis and cure, precautionary food-safety surveillance for aflatoxins, metabolic-risk assessment embedded in liver care, risk-based liver ultrasound surveillance with alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) used only as an adjunct, strengthened diagnostic imaging and pathology, and a national liver-cancer registry. Locally led epidemiological and implementation research, including population-attributable-fraction scenario modelling and representativeness analyses of existing hospital series, is urgently needed to quantify the relative contribution of viral, toxic, and metabolic pathways and to identify feasible models for surveillance and referral in a resource-constrained setting.

title: Development and External Validation of a Multimodal Machine Learning Model Integrating Preoperative Contrast-Enhanced CT Radiomics and Clinicopathological Features for Predicting Early Extrahepatic Recurrence After Hepatectomy for Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Background Early extrahepatic recurrence (eEHR) after hepatectomy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) significantly affects patient prognosis; however, an accurate predictive framework integrating radiomics with clinicopathological features is currently lacking. This study aims to develop and validate a multimodal machine learning model for prediction of early postoperative extrahepatic recurrence risk, thereby offering a basis for individualized postoperative intervention strategies. Methods A total of 208 patients who received surgical resection and had a postoperative pathological diagnosis of HCC were retrospectively enrolled from two centers between 2018 and 2023. The cohort was divided into a training set and an internal validation set at a 7:3 ratio. An external validation set was also established. Preoperative enhanced CT radiomic features and clinicopathological characteristics were extracted. After screening for key features using regression analysis, multiple machine learning prediction models were constructed via nested k-fold cross validation. The performance of the models was evaluated, and survival analysis was subsequently conducted. Results Among the 208 patients, 55 (26.4%) had postoperative eEHR. The most common site of recurrence was the lung (26 cases, 47.3%), followed by lymph nodes (12 cases, 21.8%) and bone (10 cases, 18.2%). Three core clinicopathological features and four key radiomic features were identified. A multimodal predictive model for HCC-eEHR was developed using the Random Forest algorithm. This model achieved an AUC of 0.852 (sensitivity 0.511, specificity 0.959) in the training cohort and an AUC of 0.836 (sensitivity 0.750, specificity 0.875, accuracy 0.850) in the external validation cohort. A 24-month landmark analysis (n=156) confirmed that patients developing eEHR within 24 months had significantly worse post-landmark overall survival (median 16.3 vs 47.7 months; HR=3.342, 95%CI: 1.570-7.112, P<0.001). Furthermore, the model demonstrated effective risk stratification in both cohorts (Southwest OS: HR=3.549, 95%CI: 2.097-6.006, P<0.001; Leshan OS: HR=3.839, 95%CI: 1.171-8.369, P=0.026). Conclusion The developed multimodal prediction model may assist in assessing the risk of eEHR following HCC hepatectomy, thereby facilitating the timely identification of high-risk patients and informing personalized postoperative surveillance and treatment strategies.

title: Machine Learning Model Integrating Conventional Ultrasound Radiomics and Clinicopathological Features for Early Recurrence Risk Prediction After Curative-Intent Hepatectomy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Purpose To develop and compare machine learning models integrating conventional ultrasound radiomic features with clinicopathological variables for predicting one-year postoperative recurrence in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma after curative-intent hepatectomy. Methods This retrospective, single-center study included 154 patients with pathologically confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma who underwent curative-intent hepatectomy between January 2020 and December 2024. Patients were divided into a training cohort (n = 124) and a validation cohort (n = 30). Clinicopathological data and preoperative conventional ultrasound images were collected. Radiomic features were extracted and selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Predictive models were developed and compared using conventional logistic regression and four machine learning algorithms, including a generalized linear model (GLM), random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and gradient boosting machine (GBM), based on different combinations of clinicopathological variables and radiomic features. Model performance was evaluated in the validation cohort. Results Multivariable logistic regression identified Edmondson grade, satellite nodules, fibrinogen, and white blood cell count as factors independently associated with postoperative recurrence. Among the evaluated models, the RF model combining clinicopathological factors with the Radscore achieved the highest numerical validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.717 (95% confidence interval: 0.523-0.910), with an accuracy of 70.0%, a sensitivity of 42.9%, and a specificity of 93.8%. Conclusion The RF model integrating clinicopathological factors with the Radscore showed moderate discrimination for one-year postoperative recurrence and may hold promise for postoperative risk assessment. Given the limited validation sample size and uncertainty in model performance, these findings should be considered exploratory and require further validation in larger, independent, multicenter cohorts before clinical implementation.

title: Tubercular Uveitis: Multimodal Imaging, Immunologic Stratification, and a Practical Framework for Diagnosis and Management.
abstract: Tubercular uveitis (TBU) remains difficult to diagnose and monitor because microbiologic confirmation is uncommon and clinical phenotypes overlap with other inflammatory chorioretinal disorders. This narrative review integrates evidence from multimodal imaging, immune testing, systemic tuberculosis evaluation, molecular diagnostics, biomarkers, treatment response, and monitoring to support a practical probability-based approach to suspected TBU. A targeted search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was conducted for English-language literature through May 10, 2026, prioritizing consensus statements, systematic reviews, multicenter studies, and clinically relevant imaging, biomarker, and treatment reports. Enhanced-depth and swept-source optical coherence tomography, optical coherence tomography angiography, fundus autofluorescence, indocyanine green angiography, and ultra-widefield fluorescein angiography provide complementary information on choroidal granulomas, serpiginous-like choroiditis, retinal vasculitis, ischemia, and paradoxical worsening. Tuberculin skin testing and interferon-gamma release assays support tuberculosis attribution but do not prove ocular causality, while polymerase chain reaction and emerging molecular assays increase specificity when positive. Cytokine profiles, type I interferon signatures, complement C1q, and cell-free DNA remain investigational. TBU should be managed as a clinicoradiologic and immunologic probability diagnosis that links phenotype, imaging, tuberculosis exposure evidence, mimic exclusion, antitubercular therapy decisions, anti-inflammatory timing, and longitudinal monitoring to reduce both missed TBU and unnecessary treatment.

title: Extreme Diagnostic and Therapeutic Heterogeneity Limits Treatment Conclusions in Iliotibial Band Syndrome: A Systematic Review with Level-of-Evidence Stratification.
abstract: Background Iliotibial band syndrome (ITBS) is a leading cause of lateral knee pain in runners and endurance athletes, yet clinical decision-making remains inconsistent and largely unsupported by high-quality comparative evidence. No comprehensive synthesis has previously integrated all available treatment modalities using a standardized evidence framework, and the evidence base for individual injection-based therapies continues to evolve rapidly. Objective To evaluate all available treatment strategies for ITBS and stratify their efficacy according to the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (CEBM) levels of evidence. Methods A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261374567) on 20 April 2026. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 29 April 2026. Screening, data extraction, and the subsequent review processes were completed by 21 May 2026. An updated search subsequently identified one further eligible trial, published after the original cut-off. Eligible studies included RCTs, prospective and retrospective cohort studies, and case series reporting outcomes in adults with clinically diagnosed ITBS. Studies were classified into five treatment categories: therapeutic exercise, instrumental physical therapy, manual therapy and minimally invasive techniques, injection-based, pharmacological and biologic treatments, and surgical interventions. The primary outcomes were pain reduction and functional improvement; secondary outcomes included return to sport, recurrence, quality of life, patient satisfaction, and adverse events. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool and NIH Quality Assessment Tools. Results Twenty-four studies involving 1012 patients were included. Improvements in pain and function were reported across all treatment categories. Manual therapy, corticosteroid/pharmacological injections, and platelet-rich plasma reached Level I evidence; therapeutic exercise and instrumental physical therapy Level Ib; surgical treatments Level IV. A single, adequately powered, placebo-controlled trial now provides Level I evidence for ultrasound-guided platelet-rich plasma (PRP) in refractory ITBS, whereas TECAR (Transfer of Energy Capacitive And Resistive), low-level laser, prolotherapy, and hyaluronic acid still lacked any ITBS-specific controlled evidence. Conclusion Despite a broad therapeutic landscape, most treatment modalities cannot yet be recommended over one another. To evaluate all available treatment strategies for ITBS and stratify their efficacy according to the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (CEBM) levels of evidence.

A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261374567) on 20 April 2026. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool and NIH Quality Assessment Tools.

Twenty-four studies involving 1012 patients were included. Improvements in pain and function were reported across all treatment categories. title: Utility of Vorasidenib in IDH1 R132C-Mutant WHO Grade 2 Astrocytoma: A Case Report.
abstract: WHO grade 2 astrocytomas are defined by an IDH mutation and the absence of 1p/19q codeletion. Most harbor the canonical IDH1 R132H substitution; rarer R132X variants, including R132C, remain underrepresented in prospective trials. Vorasidenib, a brain-penetrant dual IDH1/IDH2 inhibitor, prolongs progression-free survival in residual or recurrent grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma and is now included in contemporary North American guidelines when radiotherapy and chemotherapy can be deferred. We report a 25-year-old man who underwent maximal safe resection of a right temporal mass diagnosed as WHO grade 2 astrocytoma, IDH1 R132C mutant, with co-occurring ATRX and TP53 alterations. Serial postoperative MRI showed progressive residual non-enhancing T2/FLAIR signal (7 × 6 mm, then 10×7 mm, then 10×9 mm), and a 2024 biopsy confirmed residual grade 2 tumor without anaplastic features. Vorasidenib 40 mg orally once daily was started in fall 2024. After 17 months of continuous therapy (35 months after resection), the residual non-enhancing focus remains radiographically stable, and no treatment-related adverse events have occurred. Vorasidenib binds an allosteric pocket at the IDH1 dimer interface that does not directly include codon 132, which supports anticipated class activity across R132X variants. This observation is structural, not a demonstration that R132C is more sensitive than R132H. Direct comparative clinical data for R132C remain absent. This case adds real-world evidence that vorasidenib can be used safely in this uncommon molecular subgroup.

title: The Innovex RS Delivery Catheter as a Single-Platform Endoscopic System for Upper Urinary Tract Intervention: A Two-Case Report of Upper Ureteral Lithotripsy and Ablation of a Suspected Renal Pelvis Urothelial Lesion.
abstract: Background Conventional upper urinary tract endoscopy requires two instruments-a rigid ureteroscope for initial access and a flexible ureteroscope for intraluminal treatment-resulting in intraoperative scope exchange and dual-tower dependency. The Innovex RS delivery catheter is a rigid stainless-steel sheath that enables a single-use 7.5 Fr flexible ureteroscope to function in both rigid and flexible operative modes from one platform. To our knowledge this is the first report of a rigid-delivery sheath system used as the sole endoscopic instrument across two distinct upper urinary tract indications, and the first describing its use for ablation of a renal pelvis lesion. Cases Two patients underwent upper urinary tract endoscopy using the RS catheter as the sole instrument: a 53-year-old male with a 12 mm impacted proximal ureteral stone (holmium:YAG lithotripsy), and a 76-year-old female with a 10 mm renal pelvis filling defect, radiologically suspected to represent urothelial pathology on the basis of CT attenuation, who underwent cold-cup biopsy followed by thulium:YAG ablation. No rigid ureteroscope, tower switching, or fluoroscopic guidance was used in either case; this reflected operator judgement rather than any intrinsic capability of the device. Results Stone-free status was confirmed by non-contrast computed tomography on postoperative day 1 in Case 1. Macroscopic complete ablation was achieved in Case 2. Histopathological examination of the biopsy specimen demonstrated inflammatory exudate with focal urothelial mucosa and mild epithelial atypia, without definitive invasive malignancy. The ablated lesion therefore remains a radiologically suspected but histopathologically unconfirmed urothelial neoplasm, and the patient has entered a structured surveillance programme. Operative times were 55 and 90 minutes respectively; in Case 2, approximately 60 of the 90 minutes were attributable to intrapelvic clot evacuation. Clavien-Dindo grades were 0 and I respectively. Conclusion The RS delivery catheter system enabled single-platform, single-tower ureteroscopy without scope exchange in two patients. These proof-of-concept observations establish technical feasibility only. They are not sufficient to demonstrate superiority, equivalent efficacy, improved safety, or cost-effectiveness relative to the conventional two-instrument workflow, and any such advantages remain hypotheses requiring prospective comparative evaluation.

title: Anti-GQ1b-Positive Bickerstaff Brainstem Encephalitis Complicated by Diffuse Hypertrophic Pachymeningitis: A Case Report.
abstract: A 36-year-old man developed acute progressive ataxia, an impaired consciousness, and ophthalmoplegia after an upper respiratory tract infection. A cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed pleocytosis in the patient. Initial plain brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed no remarkable findings, whereas initial brain perfusion single-photon emission computed tomography demonstrated hyperperfusion in the brainstem. Follow-up contrast-enhanced MRI revealed diffuse dural thickening, and a histopathological examination supported the diagnosis of hypertrophic pachymeningitis. Anti-GQ1b antibodies were detected, leading to a diagnosis of Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis (BBE). This case suggests that hypertrophic pachymeningitis may be a rare complication of BBE.

title: Stercoral Ulcer-related Lower Rectal Perforation Associated with Persistent Rectal Fecal Impaction: Three Case Reports and Clinical Implications.
abstract: Stercoral ulcer-related lower rectal perforation is an uncommon but potentially under-recognized condition. We report three cases of elderly women with localized lower rectal perforation associated with persistent rectal fecal impaction. All patients presented with hematochezia without generalized peritonitis despite the continued passage of loose or muddy stools. Serial computed tomography revealed persistent fecal impaction in the lower rectum during the clinical course. Continued bowel movement does not necessarily indicate effective rectal evacuation. Recognition of persistent rectal fecal impaction may facilitate an earlier diagnosis and appropriate management.

title: Montmorillonite-supported Reagents: A Powerful and Versatile Platform for the Synthesis of Biologically Active Compounds Our Own Endeavor.
abstract: This review presents recent advances in montmorillonite-catalyzed organic transformations, highlighting its potential as an efficient, economical and environmentally benign solid-acid catalyst. Montmorillonite and its modified forms effectively promote a wide range of organic reactions, including multicomponent reactions, selective nitration, oxidation and reduction processes, and the synthesis of enamines, pyrroles, and β-lactams. Furthermore, integration with sustainable synthetic approaches such as microwave irradiation, ultrasound-assisted reactions, and solvent-free conditions further enhances reaction rates, improves conversions and selectivities, reduces the formation of undesirable by-products, while limiting the use of hazardous solvents. Particular emphasis is placed on hybrid catalytic systems in which metal salts, such as Bi(NO3)3 and SmI2, are supported on montmorillonite to improve catalytic activity, regioselectivity, and stereoselectivity. These methodologies demonstrate broad synthetic applicability for the preparation of pharmaceutically important compounds, including 1,4-dihydropyridines, β-lactams, aromatic amines, and nitrated derivatives of bioactive molecules such as eugenol and estradiol. Furthermore, a comparative evaluation of catalytic performance and the structural and spectroscopic characteristics of montmorillonite-based materials is also presented. Overall, montmorillonite-supported catalytic systems offer a versatile, efficient, and sustainable platform for advancing environmentally responsible organic synthesis.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence-driven Approaches in the Diagnosis and Management of Diabetes and Diabetes-Associated Complications.
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a global health issue with escalating metabolic dysfunction, clinical heterogeneity, and rising microvascular and macrovascular consequences. Traditional diabetes diagnosis, risk assessment, treatment selection, and complication surveillance rely on periodic clinical measures and population-level risk models, which may not fully capture dynamic, individualized disease pathways. Precision diabetes treatment is being transformed by Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and multimodal data analytics. This review critically examines AI-driven approaches to diabetes management, including early disease prediction, diagnostic support, glycemic monitoring, treatment-response prediction, and the prevention and detection of diabetes-associated complications. The US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) has sanctioned multiple AI/ML-based medical devices for automated retinal screening, clinical diagnostic assistance, and patient self-management applications. For clinically meaningful patterns and disease progression prediction, AI-enabled analysis of continuous glucose monitoring data, retinal images, electronic health records, wearable device signals, laboratory parameters, and multi-omics datasets is prioritized. The use of AI for detecting diabetic retinopathy, kidney disease, cardiovascular disease, neuropathy, and foot disorders is also highlighted.Data quality, algorithmic bias, interpretability, privacy, cybersecurity, model drift, regulatory monitoring, clinical validation, and equitable access prevent widespread application despite promising results. This study offers a thorough and critical assessment of the developing roles of AI, specifically ML and DL, in the prediction, diagnosis, and management of diabetes and its related complications. Real-world validation, standardized evaluation frameworks, trustworthy AI, and effective human- AI collaboration will drive advancement. AI could transform diabetes management into predictive, tailored, continuous, and complication-preventive care.

title: Current Applications and Emerging Horizons of Artificial Intelligence in Temporal Bone Computed Tomography.
abstract: The temporal bone has intricate anatomy. CT examinations can clearly depict fine anatomical structures and subtle lesions, providing indispensable imaging evidence for diagnosing otologic diseases and planning surgical procedures. However, image interpretation has several inherent limitations, including subjectivity, substantial interobserver variability, and heavy reliance on physician experience, all of which can compromise clinical decision-making and lead to inconsistent patient management. In recent years, AI-driven approaches have made significant progress in this field, particularly in optimizing image quality, identifying key anatomical structures, and assisting in the diagnosis of common otologic diseases. These advances span multiple tasks and have gradually narrowed the performance gap between automated tools and expert readers. Despite encouraging results in research settings, AI tools continue to encounter multiple obstacles in the transition from algorithmic validation to routine clinical use. These challenges include insufficient and imbalanced training data, limited generalizability across diverse populations and imaging protocols, and a persistent lack of clinician trust arising from the "black-box" nature of these models. Moreover, the absence of standardized benchmarks and prospective clinical trials further impedes the deployment of these technologies in routine otologic practice. This paper comprehensively reviews current AI applications in temporal bone CT imaging and discusses related emerging technologies, aiming to provide new perspectives and methods for clinical practice.

title: ECTU-Net: Efficient Channel Attention and Transformer Integration for Liver Tumor Segmentation in CT Images.
abstract: Background U-Net and its variants have demonstrated strong local feature extraction in medical image segmentation. Methods Efficient Channel Attention-Transformer U-Net (ECTU-Net) is proposed to recover fine boundaries and refine multi-scale features. A lightweight four-layer U-Net serves as the backbone. Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) modules enhance channel-wise feature selection, and compact Transformer blocks learn global dependencies. A Flatten-Transformer-Reshape process at the bottleneck replaces high-dimensional convolutions to capture pixel-level long-range dependencies. Results On LiTS17, ECTU-Net improves the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) by 9.20% over the original U-Net and reduces FLOPs by 42.3%. The Transformer block adds only 0.09M parameters while improving global context modeling. Discussion ECTU-Net outperforms the comparison models in liver tumor segmentation and accurately delineates tumor regions. It combines high segmentation accuracy with parameter efficiency. However, the limited sample size restricts the generalizability of the findings. Conclusion ECTU-Net enables high-precision medical image segmentation in resource-constrained settings and shows strong potential for clinical application.

title: Genital Tuberculosis (GTB): Insights into Diagnosis, Treatment, Clinical Trials and Patents-A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: Genital Tuberculosis (GTB) represents a frequently unrecognized type of extrapulmonary Tuberculosis (TB) that affects the female reproductive system. The condition results in infertility, menstrual cycle disturbances, and pelvic pain. The condition is difficult to detect at an early stage because its mild symptoms can manifest in different body parts. Therefore, medical professionals require better methods for diagnosing and treating patients. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, diagnostic approaches, therapeutic strategies, and current advancements in the management of GTB. The study presents information on New Drug Delivery systems (NDDs), current clinical trials, and new patents to guide future research. A literature-based narrative review was conducted, focusing on peer-reviewed articles, clinical studies, patents, and recent advances in diagnostics and therapeutics of GTB. The study focused on three main areas: anatomical site-specific manifestations; laboratory instruments and drug medications. The fallopian tubes are the most commonly affected site (90-100%), followed by the endometrium (50-60%), ovaries (20-30%), cervix (5-10%), while involvement of the vagina and vulva is rare (<1%). The diagnosis of GTB becomes problematic because both its visible and hidden symptoms start to appear. The development of effective detection methods depends on both traditional diagnostic methods and modern molecular methods, which include specialized laboratory equipment, imaging techniques, and histopathology. Current clinical trials and new patent approvals demonstrate the development of new methods for diagnosing and treating GTB, including improved therapeutic approaches and drug delivery systems. GTB presents both diagnostic and treatment difficulties because patients show different symptoms that can remain hidden. The combination of methods for diagnosing and treating GTB, through improved therapeutic approaches and drug-delivery systems, will enhance detection, treatment outcomes, and the ability to maintain fertility. The research should investigate personalized medicine approaches, molecular diagnostic technologies, and new therapeutic delivery systems to address the existing clinical needs in GTB treatment.

title: Prospective Evaluation of Standalone Endovascular Embolization for Growing Meningiomas: A Multicenter Study Protocol.
abstract: Endovascular embolization for meningiomas has traditionally been performed as a preoperative adjunct; however, embolization alone can induce tumor necrosis and volume reduction. This study aims to prospectively evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization in patients with growing meningiomas. This multicenter, prospective, single-arm study will include patients diagnosed with meningioma using imaging findings that showed interval growth. The primary end point is tumor growth control at 180 days after treatment, defined as a stable or reduced tumor volume based on quantitative volumetric assessment of the contrast-enhancing portion on magnetic resonance imaging. The secondary end points include the tumor volume change rate, embolized vessels, embolic materials, embolization results and characteristics, procedure-related complications, perioperative complications, functional outcomes (Karnofsky Performance Status and modified Rankin Scale), changes in clinical symptoms, and the need for additional treatment. Exploratory analyses will also assess the association between intratumoral penetration of embolic material and treatment outcomes. Patient recruitment is ongoing, and the results will be reported upon completion of the study. This study represents a prospective attempt to evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization for meningiomas. If safe tumor growth control can be achieved, this study may provide preliminary evidence supporting standalone embolization as a potential less-invasive treatment strategy.

title: Prosthetically driven implant placement assisted by tablet-based augmented reality and tooth-supported registration: A technical procedure with planned-to-placed verification.
abstract: Purpose This technical procedure describes a tablet-based augmented reality (AR) workflow for prosthetically driven single-implant placement using tooth-supported marker registration and postoperative planned-to-placed three-dimensional (3D) verification. Methods Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), intraoral scans, and digital wax-up data were integrated to generate a prosthetically driven implant plan. The planning dataset was converted into an AR-compatible model and visualized on a tablet using the TreLab software. A tooth-supported AR marker guide was fabricated for marker-based registration. During surgery, the surgeon intermittently consulted the AR overlay as a visual reference to the planned implant axis and contextual anatomy. The drill was not tracked, and the osteotomy depth and implant placement were conventionally controlled. Postoperative CBCT was performed, and planned-to-placed deviations were calculated by best-fit superimposition using the remaining teeth as the reference region. Conclusions The workflow was completed without intraoperative complications or technical interruptions. Planned-to-placed verification demonstrated an angular deviation of 3.25°, a coronal 3D deviation of 0.68 mm, and an apical 3D deviation of 0.93 mm. These results demonstrate the technical feasibility of integrating prosthetically driven implant planning, tablet-based AR visualization, tooth-supported registration, and postoperative planned-to-placed verification into a single-implant clinical workflow. Because neither the drill nor the implant was dynamically tracked and the quantitative overlay error was not measured, the findings should be interpreted as preliminary technical verification rather than as evidence of navigational accuracy or clinical superiority.

title: Prognostic Significance of PET- SUV max in Patients Undergoing Resection of Hepatocellular Carcinoma >3 cm: A Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: Background/aim Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) >3 cm often recurs after resection, indicating a need for better risk stratification. The 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) maximum standardized uptake value (SUV max ) reflects tumor aggressiveness. We evaluated the prognostic significance of preoperative FDG-PET SUV max in patients with resectable initial HCC >3 cm. Patients and methods This retrospective analysis included 136 patients who underwent curative resection for HCC >3 cm between 2012 and 2021 with preoperative FDG-PET imaging. Patients were classified into low- and high-uptake groups based on tumor SUV max . Associations between FDG-PET findings and clinicopathological factors were analyzed. Results Patients with high SUV max had significantly worse overall survival than those with low SUV max (49.2% vs . 90.0%, p <0.0001). Multivariate analysis identified high SUV max as an independent predictor of poor overall survival (hazard ratio=3.16, 95% confidence interval=1.42-7.03, p =0.0048). Furthermore, recurrence-free survival was significantly worse in the high SUV max group (33.4% vs . 60.4%, p =0.0006). High SUV max was strongly associated with microscopic vascular invasion (MVI). Combining SUV max with alpha-fetoprotein improved preoperative prediction of MVI. Conclusion Preoperative FDG-PET SUV max is an independent prognostic biomarker in HCC >3 cm and, when combined with serum alpha-fetoprotein, may enhance prediction of MVI. These findings support incorporating metabolic imaging into preoperative risk models to guide management.

title: Preoperative Prediction of Lymph Node Metastasis in Colorectal Cancer Using Routinely Collected Clinical Data: Multicenter Retrospective Machine Learning Model Development and External Validation Study.
abstract: Background Preoperative nodal assessment in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains imperfect, and uncertainty regarding pathological lymph node metastasis (LNM) may persist despite conventional imaging. Machine learning using routinely available preoperative information may provide complementary patient-level risk estimates without requiring radiomic feature extraction or molecular testing. Objective This study aimed to develop and externally validate machine learning models for preoperative estimation of pathologically confirmed LNM risk in patients with newly diagnosed CRC undergoing direct radical surgery without preoperative anticancer treatment, and to assess whether multivariable prediction adds information beyond clinical tumor stage (cT) alone. Methods This multicenter retrospective study included 2725 patients from 2 hospitals. The internal cohort (n=1074) was split into training (n=753) and internal test (n=321) sets, while 1651 patients from a second center formed the external validation cohort. Candidate predictors were routinely available preoperative clinical, laboratory, tumor-marker, imaging-based, and endoscopic biopsy variables. Predictors were selected using univariable and multivariable logistic regression (LR). Seven algorithms were evaluated: random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), LR, decision tree (DT), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), naive Bayes (NB), and light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM). Performance was assessed using discrimination, threshold-dependent classification metrics, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were used for interpretation. Sensitivity analyses compared the selected predictors with all candidate predictors and cT alone. Results Six predictors were retained: BMI, preoperative carcinoembryonic antigen, primary tumor site, cT, histological type, and tumor differentiation. RF was selected based on internal test performance. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.803 (95% CI 0.756-0.849) in the internal test set and 0.776 (95% CI 0.755-0.797) in external validation. In external validation, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were 0.687, 0.677, 0.693, 0.569, and 0.781, respectively. The Brier score was 0.190, and the calibration slope was 1.061. cT contributed most in SHAP analysis; however, the 6-predictor RF model showed significantly higher discrimination than cT alone in both the internal test set (AUROC 0.803 vs 0.712; ΔAUROC=0.091; P <.001) and external validation cohort (AUROC 0.776 vs 0.707; ΔAUROC=0.069; P <.001). Discrimination did not differ significantly between the 6-predictor and all-predictor RF models. Conclusions We developed and externally validated a 6-predictor RF model for preoperative LNM risk estimation in patients with newly diagnosed CRC undergoing radical resection with regional lymph node dissection without preoperative anticancer treatment. The model showed moderate external discrimination and provided predictive information beyond cT alone. It is intended for research-stage adjunctive risk stratification and should not replace imaging, pathological evaluation, or clinical judgment. Prospective validation in broader populations and clinical settings is required before implementation.

Six predictors were retained: BMI, preoperative carcinoembryonic antigen, primary tumor site, cT, histological type, and tumor differentiation. RF was selected based on internal test performance. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.803 (95% CI 0.756-0.849) in the internal test set and 0.776 (95% CI 0.755-0.797) in external validation. In external validation, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were 0.687, 0.677, 0.693, 0.569, and 0.781, respectively. The Brier score was 0.190, and the calibration slope was 1.061. cT contributed most in SHAP analysis; however, the 6-predictor RF model showed significantly higher discrimination than cT alone in both the internal test set (AUROC 0.803 vs 0.712; ΔAUROC=0.091; P<.001) and external validation cohort (AUROC 0.776 vs 0.707; ΔAUROC=0.069; P<.001). Discrimination did not differ significantly between the 6-predictor and all-predictor RF models.

Conclusions

We developed and externally validated a 6-predictor RF model for preoperative LNM risk estimation in patients with newly diagnosed CRC undergoing radical resection with regional lymph node dissection without preoperative anticancer treatment. The model showed moderate external discrimination and provided predictive information beyond cT alone. It is intended for research-stage adjunctive risk stratification and should not replace imaging, pathological evaluation, or clinical judgment. Prospective validation in broader populations and clinical settings is required before implementation.

title: Refined Exclusion in Medical AI: Data Justice and Patient Safety Governance.
abstract: Medical AI is often evaluated using aggregate measures of discrimination, calibration, and accuracy. However, these measures can obscure clinically important variation across patient groups, institutions, devices, and workflows. This viewpoint defines refined exclusion as a governance condition in which an AI system appears successful in aggregate, while uncertainty, error, or reduced clinical reliability is concentrated in populations that are insufficiently represented, measured, validated, or monitored. The concept does not replace algorithmic fairness, hidden stratification, dataset shift, or subgroup performance analysis. It connects these mechanisms to a distinct consequence: an unequal distribution of safety that remains inadequately detected or corrected. Drawing on purposively selected, illustrative evidence from population health management, chest radiography, dermatology, computational pathology, medical foundation models, and clinical measurement, we distinguish model-level disparity, patient safety signals, and documented patient harm. We then frame data justice as a complementary governance approach with distributional, procedural, and substantive dimensions. The proposed lifecycle decision gates address intended use, subgroup learnability, data provenance, validation, procurement, local deployment, monitoring, updates, and patient feedback. Each gate links minimum evidence to decision authority and 1 of 4 actions: proceed, enrich or validate, restrict use, or pause or retire. Governance intensity should be proportionate to clinical risk and evidentiary uncertainty. By linking subgroup evidence gaps to institutional decisions and corrective action, the framework shifts attention from whether a model performs well on average to whether its safety is demonstrable for the populations and settings in which it will be used.

title: Improving Postpolypectomy Surveillance Decisions Using an Automated Analysis of Colonoscopy and Histopathology Reports: 2-Center Validation Study.
abstract: Background Postpolypectomy surveillance intervals derived from colonoscopy findings and histopathology should be guideline-based, yet these are frequently not adhered to, contributing to under- and oversurveillance. This motivates a more structured and automated approach to improve adherence. Objective We developed and evaluated an automated, implementable, guideline-aligned decision support tool that extracts colorectal polyp features from free-text colonoscopy and histopathology reports and produces auditable surveillance recommendations. Methods We extracted paired colonoscopy and histopathology reports from a National Health Service (NHS) trust and designed a 4-stage prompting pipeline using open-weight large language models to separate multispecimen histopathology reports into individual containers ("pots"), align endoscopic findings with specimens, and normalize each pot into a structured schema. The surveillance intervals were then computed by a deterministic rule engine encoding guideline rules. We evaluated extraction performance on 100 procedures (215 pots), assessed surveillance recommendation performance on a same-site cohort (n=100), and performed external validation on a cohort from a second trust (n=100). A separate retrospective audit compared automated recommendations and observed routine scheduling against a clinician-derived reference based on full electronic health record review in 127 patients. Results Key extraction fields showed end-to-end accuracy (specimen type=0.995; location=0.981; diagnosis=0.981; excision completeness=0.949), with mean report-level pot comprehensiveness of 0.968 (SD 0.112). Overall surveillance recommendation accuracy was 0.96 (95% CI 0.90-0.98) at Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust (GSTT) and 0.93 (95% CI 0.86-0.97) at Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust (SWB) and showed strong class-level performance (no follow-up F 1 -score of 0.98 at GSTT and 0.97 at SWB; site check F 1 -score of 0.93 at GSTT and 0.91 at SWB; 3-year follow-up F 1 -score of 0.86 at GSTT and 0.80 at SWB; cancer alert F 1 -score of 1.00 at GSTT and 1.00 at SWB). The comparison to current clinical practice showed that the tool would improve guideline adherence primarily by reducing potential undersurveillance. Conclusions This hybrid approach using open-weight large language models for structured extraction and guideline-encoded rules for decision-making can generate accurate, lightweight, and auditable postpolypectomy surveillance recommendations. Such a tool has the potential to improve safety netting and guideline adherence in NHS colonoscopy workflows.

title: Reducing Annotation Costs Using Knowledge Distillation for Label‑Efficient Negation Detection in Radiology Reports: Multisite Internal Validation Study.
abstract: Background Negation in radiology reports (eg, "no evidence of dissection") is essential for accurately conveying diagnostic information. Clinical natural language processing systems, however, often fail to determine whether findings occur within negated or speculative contexts, leading to excessive false keyword alerts, noise in information extraction, and reduced precision in downstream clinical or research applications. Transformer models have advanced detection capabilities but require costly expert labeling. Large language models (LLMs) may provide label-efficient alternatives through few-shot prompting or knowledge distillation. Objective This study aims to systematically evaluate LLMs and transformer models under different supervision strategies, including comparisons of expert-labeled and LLM-distilled transformers, teacher LLMs (GPT-5.3 Chat, Gemma 4, and Qwen3.6-Plus), sampling approaches, and direct few-shot LLM inference, to determine whether LLM inference or LLM-based distillation can substitute for human labeling in radiology-report negation detection while reducing annotation costs. Methods We reused and analyzed 6000 deidentified English-language radiology reports from 3 hospital branches. Three LLMs-GPT-5.3 Chat, Gemma 4, and Qwen3.6-Plus-performed 0-, 5-, and 10-shot inference to identify negations and speculations unrelated to abnormal findings and generate pseudo-labels for transformer fine-tuning (Bio_ClinicalBERT [Bio + Clinical BERT model], BERT [Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers], and ALBERT [A Lite Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers]). We trained models using human-labeled or LLM-distilled supervision across 28 training data scales (n=42-4200) and 3 data sampling seeds and compared them across multiple supervision and training conditions encompassing backbone, label source, and sampling strategy. We assessed performance using keyword-level precision, recall, and F1-score with paired bootstrap tests (10,000 replicates). Results We refined 1000 report annotations (interrater κ=0.957) and fine-tuned 1260 transformer models. Human-labeled transformers consistently outperformed distillation-labeled ones, with the largest gap at small training scales (ΔF1-score ≈0.042; adjusted P<.001), which narrowed at larger scales (ΔF1-score ≈0.022; adjusted P<.001). Teacher model choice had minimal effect on distilled performance. All 3 human-labeled transformer backbones (BERT, ALBERT, and Bio_ClinicalBERT) achieved high keyword-level F1-scores (0.982-0.985 under their best conditions; n=4200). In the 10-shot setting, GPT-5.3 Chat (F1-score 0.974) modestly underperformed human-labeled transformers in the large-sample range (ΔF1-score=0.009; adjusted P=.047) and significantly outperformed Gemma 4 (F1-score 0.957; adjusted P=.01) and Qwen3.6-Plus (F1-score 0.950; adjusted P<.001) in the bootstrap analysis. GPT-5.3 Chat labeled reports at approximately US $0.018 per report and became less expensive than manual annotation when expert hourly wages exceeded US $0.64-1.50. Conclusions Human-supervised transformers remain the strongest baseline, but frontier LLMs such as GPT-5.3 Chat offer comparable performance with minimal supervision. LLM-based distillation offers a cost-effective alternative with only minor performance loss. Dataset scale proved more influential than sampling strategy. Additionally, superior teacher performance yielded no proportional gains through distillation, as open-weight or low-cost teachers achieved comparable results. If supported by external validation, the proposed label-efficient framework could enable accurate and affordable negation detection and rapid domain adaptation.

title: Detection of Cervical Nodal Metastasis in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Using Elastic Scattering Spectroscopy: Ex Vivo Diagnostic Modeling Study.
abstract: Background Cervical nodal metastasis remains one of the strongest determinants of treatment planning and prognosis in oral squamous cell carcinoma. Histopathology remains the reference standard, but it does not provide immediate information at the point of surgical specimen assessment. Elastic scattering spectroscopy (ESS) offers rapid, label-free optical interrogation of tissue microstructure, and may support ex vivo nodal assessment. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of ESS combined with machine learning classification for ex vivo detection of cervical lymph node metastasis in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma. Methods We conducted a single-center observational ex vivo diagnostic modeling study in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma undergoing primary tumor resection and neck dissection. A total of 3 ESS spectra were acquired from each bivalved lymph node before routine histopathological processing. Internal validation used repeated nested 5-fold cross-validation grouped by patient, so every spectrum and lymph node from a patient remained in the same fold. All preprocessing, scaling, dimensionality reduction, within-model-family configuration, and hyperparameter tuning, probability calibration where required, and decision-threshold selection were restricted to training data within the nested validation process; comparisons between candidate model families were exploratory and were based on pooled patient-grouped out-of-fold predictions. Spectrum-level probabilities were aggregated within each lymph node, and histopathology was the reference standard. Results A total of 52 patients were assessed for eligibility, 45 were included, and 280 fresh lymph nodes were assessed by ESS; 96 were pathology positive, and 184 were pathology negative. Of 840 acquired spectra, 760 passed quality control. Of the 280 nodes, 274 retained at least 2 usable spectra and comprised the analytical cohort; 6 pathology-negative nodes yielded no analyzable node-level ESS result. The hybrid model was selected because it had the highest pooled patient-grouped out-of-fold node-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), with an internally validated, exploratory estimate of 0.966 (95% CI 0.929-0.988). The same out-of-fold predictions informed model-family selection and performance reporting; this estimate does not represent independent validation of a prospectively fixed final model. At the cross-validation-derived summary threshold, secondary descriptive operating characteristics were sensitivity 93.8% (95% CI 86.4%-97.6%), specificity 95.5% (95% CI 90.1%-98.3%), accuracy 94.9% (95% CI 90.4%-97.3%), positive predictive value 91.8% (95% CI 82.9%-96.3%), and negative predictive value 96.6% (95% CI 92.4%-98.8%). The Brier score was 0.063, with calibration-in-the-large of -0.03 and a calibration slope of 0.94. Patient-level sensitivity was 96% and specificity was 90%. Pathology-positive and pathology-negative nodes also showed differences across amplitude-related and shape-related spectral features. Conclusions ESS showed promising ex vivo discrimination of metastatic cervical lymph nodes in this single-center model-development and internal-validation study. The findings support further investigation of ESS as a potential pathology-triage adjunct rather than a replacement for histopathology.
